**Merged by the operator seat** — review: Reviewed as the top of track 217's stack, and this merge carries three nodes rather than one: kb/259 now holds its own capability vocabulary plus 260 (the brief naming the bound command) and 261 (the derived grant), both merged into it bottom-up. What this node itself adds: a frozen CAPABILITIES vocabulary with a per-intent meaning, capabilityCommand(profile, intent), and loadBoard validation of an optional profile.capabilities. The promise that matters is that a board declaring nothing is byte-identically unchanged, which the profiles tests pin. Verified myself: CI green on the final head, lint clean, 1099 tests locally with the stack merged in. Two process notes worth the record. This card took three attempts, and attempt 3 was my fault: I squash-merged its parent 255 while this branch was based on it, so the content landed on main under a different sha and the branch had to reconcile against work it already contained. That is now filed as 270, which would refuse such a merge mechanically. And when I then squashed 260 into this branch, 261 conflicted against its own base for the identical reason one level down, which I fixed by hand rather than spending a fourth session on a single-line import union. The last merge into this branch used a merge commit rather than a squash so its history stayed a valid ancestor. Siblings 260 and 261 will need closing by hand: their PRs merged into this branch rather than the default one, so GitHub never linked them and the board cannot see a merged PR on a non-default base. Filed as 275., checks: green, method: squash

residual_risk: capabilityCommand has no caller yet: nothing renders a binding into a brief (#260) or derives a grant from one (#261), so the key is validated and inert until a sibling lands. Deliberate — this card was told not to do either.

hkb doctor says nothing about capabilities (no check that a bound command exists in the harness, or that a Claude binding's Skill/slash-command tool is granted). #261 owns the grant and is the natural place for that check.
The vocabulary ships with three intents chosen from the track's framing, not from a survey of boards; adding a fourth is cheap but the test makes it deliberate, which is the point.

Validation is loadBoard-only. A caller that hand-builds a cfg object (tests, hooks reading a partial config) can hold an unvalidated capabilities map; capabilityCommand degrades to null rather than trusting it.

results.summary:
A profile may now carry "capabilities": an object mapping an intent from a closed vocabulary to what THIS harness calls it, e.g. {"review": "/code-review", "goal": "/goal"}. The intent travels, the binding is local — hkb names no harness command itself, pinned by a test.

Exported vocabulary: CAPABILITIES in src/model.js — Object.freeze({ review, goal, specify }), each key mapped to a one-line prose meaning (not a command). review = a second pass over work that already exists; goal = state the outcome the work is for; specify = turn a one-liner into a spec a cold worker can execute. It is pinned in test/profiles.test.js the way GROOM_KINDS is: every key must be frozen, name-shaped, carry a >=5-word meaning with no "/" in it, and be named by a case in that file — so an intent cannot be added without saying what it means.

Resolution function: capabilityCommand(profile, intent) -> string | null, pure, exported from src/model.js. It returns the bound command string for a known intent, and null for everything else: no capabilities key, a non-object/array map, a blank or non-string binding, an unbound intent, or an intent outside CAPABILITIES. null is the ordinary answer, never a throw — an unbound intent falls back to today's prose brief. #260 should render the brief off capabilityCommand(profile, intent) and treat null as "say it in prose"; #261 should derive its grant from the same call and route it through effectiveTools(profile, task, board), never profile.allowed_tools.

Schema: profile.capabilities is optional; when present it must be a plain object whose keys are all in CAPABILITIES and whose values are non-empty strings. loadBoard (src/board.js) validates it once, next to the existing effort checks, throwing Error with exitCode 2: `profile "<name>" in <file>: unknown capability "<intent>" — must be one of review, goal, specify`, or `... "capabilities" must be an object mapping an intent to this harness's command, e.g. {"review": "/code-review"}`, or `... capability "<intent>" must name this harness's command as a non-empty string`. An UNBOUND intent is not an error — that is the difference between a capability map and a dependency.

Absent means today's behaviour: no DEFAULT_PROFILES entry binds anything, DEFAULT_KB and DEFAULT_BOARD are untouched, nothing is defaulted in, and a board with no capabilities key deep-equals DEFAULT_PROFILES with no "capabilities" anywhere in its serialization — pinned by a test. Nothing in this card touches effectiveTools, src/dispatch.js or src/context.js.

Branched from kb/255. PR: https://github.com/emyann/harness-kanban-board/pull/264 (draft, --base kb/255).
